records.source: Ἤγγιζεν δὲ ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων ἡ λεγομένη Πάσχα.
records.gloss: Was drawing near now the feast of the unleavened [bread], the [one] being called Passover.
pieces: Now the time was drawing near for the feast of Unleavened Bread, which is known as the Passover.

L.1: Now the feast of Unleavened Bread, the [one] called Passover, was drawing near.

R.1: It was almost time for the Feast of Unleavened Bread. This feast was also called the Passover.

decisions.choice: the feast of Unleavened Bread, called Passover: one festival season under two names
alternatives: two separate feasts at different times
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb was killed on the fourteenth day of the first month and eaten that night; the seven days of eating bread made without yeast followed at once (Exodus 12:1-20; Leviticus 23:5-8). Because they ran together, the whole season could be called by either name. It remembered how God brought Israel out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: was drawing near: the feast was close but had not yet begun
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures the feast approaching. It arrives in 22:7.

records.heading: The leaders plot, and Judas joins them

records.source: καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὸ πῶς ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν, ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν.
records.gloss: And were seeking the chief priests and the scribes the how they might put to death him, they were afraid for of the people.
pieces: The chief priests and the scribes were looking for some way to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, because they were afraid of the people.

L.2: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, for they feared the people.

R.2: The chief priests and the teachers of the law were trying to find a way to kill Jesus. But they were afraid of what the people might do.

decisions.choice: put to death: kill, here by having him executed
alternatives: get rid of in some other way
decisions.reason: The verb means to do away with someone, usually by killing. The leaders' plan has been growing since 19:47-48 and 20:19.

decisions.choice: they feared the people: the crowds who listened to Jesus in the temple
decisions.reason: Luke has just said that all the people came early to hear him in the temple (21:38). An open arrest during the feast might start a riot, so they needed to take him quietly (22:6).

decisions.choice: afraid of what the people might do
decisions.reason: Readable says what the leaders feared from the people (m2).

records.source: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ Σατανᾶς εἰς Ἰούδαν τὸν καλούμενον Ἰσκαριώτην, ὄντα ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τῶν δώδεκα·
records.gloss: Entered then Satan into Judas the [one] being called Iscariot, being of the number of the Twelve;
pieces: Then Satan entered into Judas, the one called Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve.

L.3: Then Satan entered into Judas, the [one] called Iscariot, who was of the number of the Twelve.

R.3: Then Satan went into Judas, the one called Iscariot. Judas was one of the twelve apostles.

decisions.choice: Satan entered Judas: Satan took hold of him and used him
alternatives: only a figure of speech for Judas' own evil choice
decisions.reason: Luke says plainly that Satan was at work, yet Judas still acts and is held responsible (22:22). After testing Jesus in the wilderness, the devil left him until a fitting time (4:13); now he returns. John says the same of Judas at the supper (John 13:2, 27).

decisions.choice: Iscariot: a second name that marked Judas off from the other Judas among the Twelve
alternatives: a known meaning such as "man of Kerioth"
decisions.reason: There was another apostle named Judas (6:16). What "Iscariot" meant is not certain; one common view is "man from Kerioth", a town in Judea (Joshua 15:25).

decisions.choice: of the number of the Twelve: one of the inner circle Jesus chose
decisions.reason: Luke stresses that the betrayer came from the twelve whom Jesus named apostles (6:13-16).

decisions.choice: the twelve apostles
decisions.reason: Readable says who "the Twelve" were (6:13).

records.source: καὶ ἀπελθὼν συνελάλησεν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ στρατηγοῖς τὸ πῶς αὐτοῖς παραδῷ αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And having gone away he spoke with the chief priests and captains the how to them he might hand over him.
pieces: He went off and talked with the chief priests and the temple officers about how he could betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to them.

L.4: And going away, he discussed with the chief priests and captains how he might hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to them.

R.4: Judas went to the chief priests and the officers of the temple guard. He talked with them about how he could help them arrest Jesus.

decisions.choice: captains: the officers of the temple guard
decisions.reason: The word can mean a military or civil officer. Here, as in 22:52 where they are called captains of the temple, they are the officers of the Levites who kept order in the temple, under the chief priests (Acts 4:1; 5:24-26).

decisions.choice: hand over: deliver Jesus into the power of his enemies
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when Jesus says the Son of Man will be handed over to people (9:44; 18:32).

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand someone over to others. Luke uses it for the Son of Man being handed over (9:44; 18:32) and for what Judas does. Literal keeps "hand over" so that the link can be seen; Balanced and Readable say "betray", since a friend handing Jesus to his enemies is a betrayal.

decisions.choice: help them arrest Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what handing him over meant in practice.

records.source: καὶ ἐχάρησαν καὶ συνέθεντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι.
records.gloss: And they rejoiced and agreed him money to give.
pieces: They were glad and agreed to pay him money.

L.5: And they rejoiced and agreed to give him money.

R.5: The leaders were very pleased. They agreed to pay Judas.

decisions.choice: money: literally silver, the common word for money
decisions.reason: Luke does not give the sum. Matthew says it was thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:15).

decisions.choice: rejoiced: they were glad
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for joy elsewhere in Luke; here it shows the leaders' delight that one of Jesus' own men offered to help them.

records.source: καὶ ἐξωμολόγησεν, καὶ ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν τοῦ παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν ἄτερ ὄχλου αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And he consented, and was seeking opportunity to hand over him apart from crowd to them.
pieces: He accepted, and from then on he looked for a good chance to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to them when no crowd was around.

L.6: And he agreed, and he was seeking an opportunity to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to them apart from a crowd.

R.6: Judas agreed. From then on he watched for a good time to hand Jesus over to them, when there was no crowd around.

decisions.choice: agreed: he accepted their offer and committed himself
decisions.reason: The verb can mean confess or praise; here, after an offer of money, it means he consented.

decisions.choice: apart from a crowd: where no crowd was present
decisions.reason: The words explain how the leaders' fear of the people (22:2) would be met: the arrest had to happen out of sight of the crowds.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand someone over to others. Luke uses it for the Son of Man being handed over (9:44; 18:32) and for what Judas does. Literal keeps "hand over" so that the link can be seen; Balanced and Readable say "betray", since a friend handing Jesus to his enemies is a betrayal.

decisions.choice: hand Jesus over
decisions.reason: Readable says "hand over" here, where the plan was to deliver him to the leaders.

records.source: Ἦλθεν δὲ ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν ἀζύμων, ᾗ ἔδει θύεσθαι τὸ πάσχα·
records.gloss: Came then the day of the unleavened [bread], on which it was necessary to be sacrificed the Passover [lamb];
pieces: Then came the day of Unleavened Bread, the day when the Passover lamb had to be killed as a sacrifice.

L.7: Then the day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover [lamb] had to be sacrificed.

R.7: Then the day came when the bread without yeast was eaten and the Passover lamb was killed as a sacrifice.

decisions.choice: the Passover had to be sacrificed: the lambs were killed at the temple on the afternoon of the fourteenth day of the month
decisions.reason: The law set the day (Exodus 12:6; Deuteronomy 16:5-6). The meal was eaten that evening, after sunset, which counted as the start of the next day.

decisions.choice: the Passover: here the lamb killed for the meal
decisions.reason: The word can mean the feast, the meal or the lamb. With "sacrificed" it means the lamb.

decisions.choice: lamb
decisions.reason: The word "lamb" is supplied, in brackets at Literal, to make clear what was killed (m2).

records.heading: Preparing the Passover

records.source: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην εἰπών· Πορευθέντες ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν τὸ πάσχα ἵνα φάγωμεν.
records.gloss: And he sent Peter and John having said, Having gone prepare for us the Passover that we may eat.
pieces: So Jesus sent Peter and John with these instructions: "Go and get the Passover meal ready for us to eat."

L.8: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent Peter and John, saying, "Go [and] prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat [it]."

R.8: Jesus sent Peter and John. He told them, "Go and prepare the Passover meal for us, so that we can eat it together."

decisions.choice: prepare the Passover: get the lamb killed at the temple and make ready the meal and the room
decisions.reason: Preparing meant taking the lamb to the temple to be killed, roasting it, and setting out unleavened bread, wine, bitter herbs and the other foods of the meal (Exodus 12:8).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ θέλεις ἑτοιμάσωμεν;
records.gloss: They and said to him, Where do you want [that] we should prepare?
pieces: They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to get it ready?"

L.9: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to prepare [it]?"

R.9: They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to prepare it?"

decisions.choice: where: the meal had to be eaten inside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: By custom the Passover was eaten within the city, and it was crowded with pilgrims, so a room had to be found.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἰδοὺ εἰσελθόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν πόλιν συναντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν εἰς ἣν εἰσπορεύεται.
records.gloss: He and said to them, Look, having entered of you into the city will meet you a man a jar of water carrying; follow him into the house into which he enters.
pieces: He told them, "As you go into the city, you will be met by a man who is carrying a jar of water. Follow him into whatever house he goes into.

L.10: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Look, when you have entered the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house that he enters.

R.10: Jesus said to them, "When you go into the city, a man carrying a jar of water will come to meet you. Follow him to the house he goes into.

decisions.choice: a man carrying a jar of water: an unusual sight that would make him easy to recognize
alternatives: an ordinary sight with no meaning
decisions.reason: Fetching water in jars was usually women's work; men more often carried water in skins. A man with a jar would stand out in the crowd.

decisions.choice: will meet you: Jesus tells beforehand what will happen
alternatives: a meeting Jesus had arranged in secret
decisions.reason: Luke does not say whether Jesus had arranged this or foresaw it. Either way the disciples find everything as he had said (22:13), as with the colt in 19:30-32.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: καὶ ἐρεῖτε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ τῆς οἰκίας· Λέγει σοι ὁ διδάσκαλος· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμα ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;
records.gloss: And you will say to the master of the house, Says to you the Teacher, Where is the guest room where the Passover with the disciples of me I may eat?
pieces: Say to the owner of the house, 'The Teacher asks you, "Which is the guest room where I can eat the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples?"'

L.11: And you will say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher says to you, "Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples?"'

R.11: Then say to the owner of the house, 'The Teacher wants to know, "Where is the guest room? I want to eat the Passover meal there with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples."'

decisions.choice: guest room: a room in a house set aside for guests
decisions.reason: This is the word used in 2:7, where there was no place for Mary and Joseph in the guest room. At his birth there was no room for Jesus; now a room is ready for him, and in it he gives himself for his disciples. Luke uses a different word for an inn (10:34).

decisions.choice: the master of the house: the owner, who would lend a room to pilgrims for the feast
alternatives: a servant in charge of the house
decisions.reason: Households in Jerusalem made rooms available to pilgrims who came for Passover. The owner is expected to know who "the Teacher" is, which suggests he was a follower or friend.

decisions.choice: The Teacher says to you: a message passed on in Jesus' name
alternatives: a request the disciples make for themselves
decisions.reason: The disciples are to speak for Jesus, giving his words as his messengers.

records.source: κἀκεῖνος ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον· ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε.
records.gloss: And that one you will show an upper room large having been spread; there prepare.
pieces: He will show you a large room upstairs, with everything laid out. Get the meal ready there."

L.12: And that [man] will show you a large upper room, furnished; prepare [it] there."

R.12: He will take you upstairs and show you a large room. It will have couches and cushions set out for a meal. Get everything ready there."

decisions.choice: furnished: spread with couches or rugs and cushions for guests to recline at the meal
decisions.reason: The word means spread or laid out. At a festive meal people lay on couches or cushions around a low table (22:14).

decisions.choice: upper room: a room built on the flat roof or on the upper floor of a house
alternatives: a room in a public building
decisions.reason: Larger houses had a room upstairs that could hold many guests. Luke uses a similar word for the upstairs room where the disciples met after the ascension (Acts 1:13), but it is not certain they were the same room.

decisions.choice: couches and cushions set out for a meal
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a furnished dining room was like (m1).

records.source: ἀπελθόντες δὲ εὗρον καθὼς εἰρήκει αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.
records.gloss: Having gone away then they found as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
pieces: So they went off and found it all just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said, and they got the Passover ready.

L.13: And going away, they found [it] just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had told them, and they prepared the Passover.

R.13: So they went. They found everything just as Jesus had told them. And they prepared the Passover meal there.

decisions.choice: as he had told them: Jesus' word comes true
decisions.reason: Luke repeats this phrase from 19:32. What Jesus foretells happens, which prepares the reader for the hard things he foretells at this meal (22:21, 34).

records.source: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡ ὥρα, ἀνέπεσεν καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι σὺν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And when came the hour, he reclined and the apostles with him.
pieces: When the hour came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table, and the apostles with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.14: And when the hour came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reclined [at table], and the apostles with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.14: When it was time for the meal, Jesus lay down at the table, and the apostles with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: reclined: lay on couches or cushions around the table, as at a festive meal
decisions.reason: At a formal meal, and at Passover above all, guests lay on their left side with their heads toward the table. Reclining at Passover was a sign of free people, no longer slaves.

decisions.choice: the hour: the appointed time for the Passover meal, after sunset
decisions.reason: First of all the hour is the time of the meal. Luke also uses "hour" for the moment of the leaders' power at his arrest (22:53).

decisions.choice: the apostles: the Twelve
decisions.reason: Luke calls the Twelve apostles (6:13). He does not name anyone else at this meal.

decisions.choice: [at table]
decisions.reason: Literal adds in brackets where they reclined, since the verb alone is unclear.

records.heading: The Passover meal with the apostles

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα φαγεῖν μεθ’ ὑμῶν πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν·
records.gloss: And he said to them, With desire I have desired this the Passover to eat with you before the me to suffer;
pieces: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "How I have longed to eat this Passover with you before I suffer!

L.15: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.

R.15: Jesus said to them, "I have wanted very much to eat this Passover meal with you before I suffer.

decisions.choice: with desire I have desired: I have longed very much
decisions.reason: Repeating the verb with its noun is a Hebrew way of making the verb stronger, found in the Greek Old Testament (Genesis 31:30). The word for desire here is a good longing, not a wrong one.

decisions.choice: before I suffer: before his death
decisions.reason: Jesus has foretold that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be killed (9:22; 17:25). Luke uses "suffer" for his death (24:26, 46).

decisions.choice: How I have longed
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the strength of the repeated verb (m1) with an exclamation.

records.source: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ φάγω αὐτὸ ἕως ὅτου πληρωθῇ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: I say for to you that not not I will eat it until when it is fulfilled in the kingdom of the God.
pieces: For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it finds its fulfillment in the kingdom of God."

L.16: For I tell you that I will certainly not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."

R.16: I tell you, I will not eat this meal again until it comes true in the kingdom of God."

decisions.choice: I will not eat it, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: I will no longer eat it, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a word meaning "no longer". Several early ones do not have it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: will not eat it until: this is the last Passover he will eat before the kingdom comes
alternatives: Jesus refuses to eat this Passover at all
decisions.reason: The strong double negative can be read as a vow not to eat this meal, so that Jesus fasts while the others eat. More likely, after saying how he longed to eat it with them (22:15), he means he will not eat it again. The words for "again" in Balanced and Readable express this reading.

decisions.choice: fulfilled in the kingdom of God: the Passover points ahead to what God will do
decisions.reason: Passover remembered the rescue from Egypt. Jesus says it will reach its full meaning in the kingdom of God, pictured as a feast (13:29; 14:15; 22:30).

decisions.choice: again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "again" to give the more likely sense (m2), even though the SBLGNT does not have the word "no longer" (m1).

records.source: καὶ δεξάμενος ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας εἶπεν· Λάβετε τοῦτο καὶ διαμερίσατε εἰς ἑαυτούς·
records.gloss: And having received a cup, having given thanks he said, Take this and divide [it] among yourselves;
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took a cup, gave thanks, and said, "Take this and share it among yourselves.

L.17: And receiving a cup [and] giving thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Take this and divide [it] among yourselves.

R.17: Then Jesus took a cup of wine and thanked God for it. He said, "Take this and share it with each other.

decisions.choice: a cup: one of the cups of wine shared during the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Luke mentions two cups, one here before the bread and one after supper (22:20). Later Jewish writings describe four cups of wine at the Passover meal; how fixed that order was in Jesus' day is not certain.

decisions.choice: giving thanks: blessing God for the wine, as was done at every meal
decisions.reason: Before drinking or eating, Jews thanked God the giver. The verb is the one from which "Eucharist" comes.

decisions.choice: a cup of wine; thanked God for it
decisions.reason: Readable says what was in the cup and to whom thanks were given.

records.source: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως οὗ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἔλθῃ.
records.gloss: I say for to you, not not I will drink from the now from the fruit of the vine until that the kingdom of the God comes.
pieces: I tell you, from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."

L.18: For I tell you, from now on I will certainly not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."

R.18: I tell you, I will not drink wine again until the kingdom of God comes."

decisions.choice: the fruit of the vine: wine
alternatives: grape juice as opposed to wine
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from the Jewish blessing said over wine, which thanks God for creating the fruit of the vine.

decisions.choice: until the kingdom of God comes: Jesus looks past his death to the coming of the kingdom
alternatives: a promise to drink with them the next day
decisions.reason: As in 22:16, Jesus speaks of a coming feast in the kingdom. He will not share this cup again until then.

decisions.choice: wine
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase (m1).

records.source: καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν διδόμενον· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
records.gloss: And having taken bread, having given thanks he broke and gave to them saying, This is the body of me the [one] for you being given; this do in the my remembrance.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took bread, and after giving thanks {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke it and handed it to them, saying, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.19: And taking bread [and] giving thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke [it] and gave [it] to them, saying, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.19: Then Jesus took some bread and thanked God for it. He broke it and gave it to them. He said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body. It is given for you. Do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: the longer text, with "which is given for you" and the whole of 22:20 (SBLGNT, in square brackets)
alternatives: the shorter text, which ends with "This is my body" and leaves out the rest of 22:19 and all of 22:20
other short forms that move the cup of 22:17-18 after the bread
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts have the longer text, among them early ones such as Papyrus 75, Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus and Codex Alexandrinus. The shorter text is found in Codex Bezae and in some Old Latin manuscripts; some Old Latin and Old Syriac witnesses have other forms that put the cup after the bread. The SBLGNT prints the longer words in square brackets to show that their place in the text is doubted. The shorter text is harder to explain as a change, since it leaves a meal with the cup before the bread; the longer text has the wide and early support. The longer words are close to Paul's account in 1 Corinthians 11:24-25. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: giving thanks: thanking God for the bread, as at every meal
decisions.reason: As in 22:17, Jesus says the thanksgiving to God that began a Jewish meal.

decisions.choice: given for you: his body handed over to death for their sake
decisions.reason: "For you" means for your good, in your place. It points to his death the next day, as the cup does (22:20), and echoes the servant of Isaiah 53 who bears the sins of many, the passage Jesus quotes in 22:37.

decisions.choice: in remembrance of me: to remember me, by doing this
decisions.reason: Passover was a remembrance of the exodus (Exodus 12:14). Jesus tells the apostles to repeat this meal to remember him and what he does for them.

decisions.choice: to remember me
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words; Literal and Balanced keep the familiar phrase, which is close to the Greek.

records.source: καὶ τὸ ποτήριον ὡσαύτως μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐν τῷ αἵματί μου, τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐκχυννόμενον.
records.gloss: And the cup likewise after the having supped, saying, This the cup [is] the new covenant in the blood of me, the [one] for you being poured out.
pieces: In the same way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the cup after the meal, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood, poured out for you.

L.20: And [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did] likewise with the cup after they had eaten, saying, "This cup [is] the new covenant in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood, which is poured out for you.

R.20: After the meal Jesus did the same with the cup. He said, "This cup is God's new covenant, made by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood. My blood is poured out for you.

decisions.choice: this verse is part of the text (SBLGNT, in square brackets)
alternatives: left out in the shorter text
decisions.reason: The whole verse is missing from the shorter text described at 22:19. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the new covenant: the covenant God promised through Jeremiah
alternatives: a new agreement among the disciples
decisions.reason: God promised a new covenant in which he would write his law on hearts and forgive sins (Jeremiah 31:31-34). The covenant at Sinai was sealed with blood (Exodus 24:8). Jesus says the new covenant is made by his blood.

decisions.choice: which is poured out for you: his blood, shed in death
decisions.reason: In the Greek the words "poured out" agree in form with "cup" rather than "blood", but the cup stands for his blood. The pouring out of blood means a violent death, and "for you" means for their sake (22:19).

decisions.choice: after they had eaten: after the main meal
decisions.reason: This cup came at the end of the meal, after the bread, when a final cup of blessing was drunk.

decisions.choice: [he did] likewise with (L); in the same way he took (B); did the same with (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb here; the verbs of 22:19 are understood. Literal brackets them.

decisions.choice: God's new covenant, made by my blood
alternatives: the new covenant in my blood
decisions.reason: Readable explains whose covenant it is and how the blood makes it (m2).

records.source: πλὴν ἰδοὺ ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ παραδιδόντος με μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης·
records.gloss: But look, the hand of the [one] handing over me [is] with me on the table;
pieces: Yet the hand of the man who is betraying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is here with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the table.

L.21: But look, the hand of the one handing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over [is] with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the table.

R.21: But the man who is going to betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is here, eating at this table with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: the hand ... on the table: the betrayer is sharing this meal
alternatives: only that his hand happens to lie there
decisions.reason: To eat with someone was a bond of friendship. The psalmist grieves over a close friend who shared his bread and turned against him (Psalm 41:10). That makes the betrayal worse.

decisions.choice: the one handing me over: the betrayal is already under way
alternatives: the one who will one day betray me
decisions.reason: The present participle shows Judas has already agreed to it (22:4-6).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the man ... eating at this table
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hand on the table (m1).

records.source: ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς μὲν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου κατὰ τὸ ὡρισμένον πορεύεται, πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ παραδίδοται.
records.gloss: For the Son indeed of the man according to the having been determined goes, but woe to the man that through whom he is handed over.
pieces: The Son of Man is going the way that has been marked out for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But how terrible it will be for that man who betrays {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

L.22: For the Son of Man indeed goes according to what has been determined, but woe to that man through whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is handed over!"

R.22: The Son of Man will die, just as God has planned. But how terrible it will be for the man who betrays {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: goes according to what has been determined: his death happens by God's plan
alternatives: by the plan of his enemies
decisions.reason: "Determined" means fixed beforehand. Luke says the same in Acts 2:23: Jesus was handed over by God's set plan and foreknowledge, yet those who killed him did wrong.

decisions.choice: goes: goes away to his death
decisions.reason: "Go" is used for departing this life, as Jesus' journey to Jerusalem has been leading to his death (9:51; 13:33).

decisions.choice: woe to that man: God's plan does not excuse the betrayer
decisions.reason: "Woe" is a cry of grief and warning (6:24-26; 17:1). God's plan and human guilt stand side by side.

decisions.choice: how terrible it will be for
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid the old word "woe", as elsewhere in Luke.

decisions.choice: will die, just as God has planned
alternatives: goes according to what has been determined
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "goes" means (m2) and who determined it (m1).

decisions.choice: handed over (L); betrays (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 22:4, Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb.

records.source: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς τὸ τίς ἄρα εἴη ἐξ αὐτῶν ὁ τοῦτο μέλλων πράσσειν.
records.gloss: And they began to discuss among themselves the who then it might be of them the [one] this being about to do.
pieces: They began to ask one another which of them it could possibly be who was going to do such a thing.

L.23: And they began to question among themselves which of them it could be who was about to do this.

R.23: The apostles began to ask each other, "Which one of us would do this?"

decisions.choice: who then it might be: they could not guess who it was
decisions.reason: The optative mood with "then" makes a doubtful question. None of them knew.

decisions.choice: a direct question
alternatives: which of them it could be
decisions.reason: Readable turns the indirect question into the words they might have said.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ καὶ φιλονεικία ἐν αὐτοῖς, τὸ τίς αὐτῶν δοκεῖ εἶναι μείζων.
records.gloss: There was then also a dispute among them, the which of them seems to be greater.
pieces: A quarrel also broke out among them over which of them was to be thought the greatest.

L.24: And there was also a dispute among them, as to which of them seemed to be greater.

R.24: Then the apostles started to argue about which of them was the most important.

decisions.choice: dispute: a quarrel driven by love of winning
decisions.reason: The word means a love of strife, a contest. It comes right after the talk of betrayal, which makes it the more shameful.

decisions.choice: greater: the greatest, the one ranked first
decisions.reason: Greek often uses the comparative form for the superlative. They argue about rank among themselves, as in 9:46.

decisions.choice: seemed to be: was regarded as
alternatives: only appeared to be, but was not
decisions.reason: The verb means to be thought of or reckoned. Their question is about standing in others' eyes.

records.heading: The greatest is the one who serves

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οἱ βασιλεῖς τῶν ἐθνῶν κυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἐξουσιάζοντες αὐτῶν εὐεργέται καλοῦνται.
records.gloss: He and said to them, The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those exercising authority over them benefactors are called.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "The kings of the Gentiles act as lords over their people, and those who hold power over them are given the title 'Benefactor'.

L.25: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors.

R.25: Jesus said to them, "The kings of the other nations rule over their people like masters. And men in power are honored with the title 'Benefactor', which means one who does good to others.

decisions.choice: benefactors: a title of honor given to rulers and rich patrons
alternatives: a plain description of kind rulers
decisions.reason: Cities set up inscriptions calling kings and wealthy men "Benefactor" for their gifts, and some kings took it as part of their name. The title praised generosity, but it also put the giver above those who owed him thanks.

decisions.choice: are called: are given the title, or perhaps call themselves
decisions.reason: The form can be passive or middle. Either way the point is the same: rulers are honored for using power over others.

decisions.choice: lord it over: rule as masters
decisions.reason: The verb is built on the word for lord or master. It is not always harsh, but here it is set against serving (22:26).

decisions.choice: which means one who does good to others
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title (m1).

decisions.choice: the other nations
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for peoples who were not Jews.

records.source: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλ’ ὁ μείζων ἐν ὑμῖν γινέσθω ὡς ὁ νεώτερος, καὶ ὁ ἡγούμενος ὡς ὁ διακονῶν·
records.gloss: You but not thus, but the greater among you let him become as the younger, and the [one] leading as the [one] serving;
pieces: With you it must not be this way. Instead, the greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the one in charge like the one who waits on others.

L.26: But you [are] not so; rather, let the greatest among you become as the youngest, and the one who leads as the one who serves.

R.26: But you must not be like them. The most important person among you should act like the youngest. The leader should be like a servant.

decisions.choice: the youngest: the one with the lowest place, who did the humble tasks
decisions.reason: In that culture age gave rank. The youngest served the older ones and took the last place.

decisions.choice: the one who serves: the one who waits on people at table
decisions.reason: The verb is used for serving food at a meal (10:40; 12:37; 17:8), which fits the setting of the Last Supper and leads into 22:27.

decisions.choice: you not so: a command, not only a description
alternatives: a statement that they are already different
decisions.reason: There is no verb. The next words are commands, so this is best read as a command too.

decisions.choice: a servant
decisions.reason: Readable uses a single word; this is the verb for serving, not the word for slave.

records.source: τίς γὰρ μείζων, ὁ ἀνακείμενος ἢ ὁ διακονῶν;
records.gloss: Who for [is] greater, the [one] reclining or the [one] serving?
pieces: Think about it: who is greater, the guest who lies at the table, or the one who serves the meal?

L.27: For who [is] greater, the one reclining [at table] or the one serving?

R.27: Who is more important, the person eating at the table or the one serving the food?

decisions.choice: the one reclining: the guest at a meal
decisions.reason: Guests lay at the table (22:14) while servants brought the food.

decisions.choice: Think about it
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the force of "for", which brings a reason, as a call to consider.

records.source: οὐχὶ ὁ ἀνακείμενος;
records.gloss: Not the [one] reclining?
pieces: Surely the one at the table.

R.27: Everyone would say it is the one eating.

decisions.choice: not the one reclining?: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The negative used here expects agreement. By the world's measure, the guest is greater.

decisions.choice: a statement
alternatives: Is it not the one at the table?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the answer the question expects (m1).

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν εἰμι ὡς ὁ διακονῶν.
records.gloss: I but in midst of you am as the [one] serving.
pieces: Yet here I am among you as the one who serves.

L.27: But I am in [the] midst of you as the one serving.

R.27: But I am here with you as one who serves you.

decisions.choice: I am among you as the one serving: Jesus turns the order upside down
alternatives: he only played the part of a servant this once
decisions.reason: Jesus, their Lord and teacher, takes the servant's place, as he pictures the master who serves his slaves in 12:37. John tells how he washed their feet at this meal (John 13:4-15).

records.source: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε οἱ διαμεμενηκότες μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐν τοῖς πειρασμοῖς μου·
records.gloss: You and are those having remained with me in the trials of me;
pieces: You are the ones who have stood by {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} trials.

L.28: And you are those who have remained with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} trials.

R.28: You have stayed with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hard times.

decisions.choice: trials: hardships and tests
decisions.reason: The word can mean temptation (22:40) or trial. Here it means the opposition and testing Jesus met during his work, which the apostles shared.

decisions.choice: have remained: they stayed loyal, and still are with him
decisions.reason: The perfect tense looks at their loyalty up to now. Jesus praises them even though he knows they will soon fail (22:34, 45).

records.source: κἀγὼ διατίθεμαι ὑμῖν, καθὼς διέθετό μοι ὁ πατήρ μου βασιλείαν, ἵνα ἔσθητε καὶ πίνητε ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης μου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ μου, καὶ καθήσεσθε ἐπὶ θρόνων τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς κρίνοντες τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: And I assign to you, as assigned to me the Father of me a kingdom, \v 30 so that you may eat and may drink at the table of me in the kingdom of me, and you will sit on thrones the twelve tribes judging of the Israel.
pieces: And just as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father has granted {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a kingdom, so I grant one to you.
You will eat and drink at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} kingdom, and you will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

L.29: And I assign to you, just as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father assigned to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, a kingdom,
L.30: so that you may eat and drink at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} kingdom, and you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

R.29: My Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a kingdom. In the same way, I am giving you a share in ruling it.
R.30: You will eat and drink at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} kingdom. And you will sit on thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: assign: grant by a solemn arrangement
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for covenant in 22:20 and can mean to make a covenant or a will. Here it means to grant or hand on. The link with the new covenant may be intended.

decisions.choice: I assign to you a kingdom: the kingdom is the object of both verbs
alternatives: I make a covenant with you, as my Father gave me a kingdom, that you may eat
decisions.reason: The word "kingdom" comes at the end of the clause about the Father, but it belongs to both: as the Father granted Jesus a kingdom, Jesus grants it to them. Another reading takes Jesus' gift to be the right to eat and drink at his table.

decisions.choice: sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes: share in ruling God's people
decisions.reason: "Judging" can mean ruling, as Israel's judges ruled. The twelve apostles stand for a renewed Israel under Jesus' rule (Matthew 19:28).

decisions.choice: eat and drink at my table: share the feast of the kingdom
decisions.reason: Eating at a king's table was an honor (2 Samuel 9:7). The kingdom is pictured as a feast (13:29; 14:15).

decisions.choice: the Father's gift first, then Jesus' gift
alternatives: I assign to you, as my Father assigned to me, a kingdom
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the Father's gift first so the sentence reads clearly.

decisions.choice: a share in ruling it
decisions.reason: Readable explains what it means for the apostles to receive a kingdom (m3).

records.source: Σίμων Σίμων, ἰδοὺ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐξῃτήσατο ὑμᾶς τοῦ σινιάσαι ὡς τὸν σῖτον·
records.gloss: Simon, Simon, look, the Satan demanded to have you to sift as the wheat;
pieces: Simon, Simon, Satan has demanded to have all of you, to sift you like wheat.

L.31: Simon, Simon, look, Satan has demanded [to have] you, to sift [you] like wheat.

R.31: Simon, Simon, listen! Satan has asked to have all of you. He wants to shake you the way a farmer shakes wheat to sift it.

decisions.choice: no introduction (SBLGNT)
alternatives: many later manuscripts begin with "And the Lord said"
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts have no words of introduction, so Jesus' speech runs on from 22:30. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: you: all of you, the apostles
decisions.reason: The pronoun is plural. Satan wants all of them; Jesus prays for Simon in particular (22:32, where "you" is singular).

decisions.choice: demanded: asked for and obtained permission
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask for someone to be handed over. As in Job 1-2, Satan can test God's people only with God's leave.

decisions.choice: to sift like wheat: to shake them hard, testing them to see what falls away
decisions.reason: Grain was shaken in a sieve to separate it from dirt and chaff. Satan wants to shake their faith with trouble (Amos 9:9).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the way a farmer shakes wheat to sift it
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m4).

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐδεήθην περὶ σοῦ ἵνα μὴ ἐκλίπῃ ἡ πίστις σου· καὶ σύ ποτε ἐπιστρέψας στήρισον τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου.
records.gloss: I but begged for you that not may fail the faith of you; and you once having turned back strengthen the brothers of you.
pieces: But I have prayed for you, so that your faith will not give out. And you, once you have turned back, must strengthen your brothers."

L.32: But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and you, when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers."

R.32: But I have prayed for you, Simon. I asked that your faith would not fail. When you have come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, help your brothers to stand firm."

decisions.choice: you: Simon alone
decisions.reason: These pronouns are singular, unlike "you" in 22:31. Jesus prays for Simon, who will deny him and then be restored.

decisions.choice: turned back: come back after failing
alternatives: been converted for the first time
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn around or return. Jesus foresees Peter's denial and his return.

decisions.choice: your brothers: the other apostles and fellow believers
decisions.reason: Peter later strengthens the believers (Acts 1:15; 2:14). Here the word means the men around the table, so no gender alternative is given.

decisions.choice: fail: give out, die away
decisions.reason: The verb is used of something running out (16:9). Peter's courage fails, but his faith is not lost.

decisions.choice: come back to me; Simon
decisions.reason: Readable names Simon and says to whom he returns (m2).

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μετὰ σοῦ ἕτοιμός εἰμι καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ εἰς θάνατον πορεύεσθαι.
records.gloss: He and said to him, Lord, with you ready I am both to prison and to death to go.
pieces: Peter answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, I am ready to go to prison with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and even to die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.33: And he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I am ready to go both to prison and to death."

R.33: Peter said, "Lord, I am ready to go to prison with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I am even ready to die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

decisions.choice: with you: placed first for emphasis
decisions.reason: Peter puts "with you" first: whatever happens to Jesus, he will share it.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λέγω σοι, Πέτρε, οὐ φωνήσει σήμερον ἀλέκτωρ ἕως τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ εἰδέναι.
records.gloss: He and said, I tell you, Peter, not will crow today a rooster until three times me you will deny knowing.
pieces: Jesus replied, "I tell you, Peter, before a rooster crows today, you will have said three times that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.34: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today until you deny three times that you know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.34: Jesus answered, "Peter, I tell you, before the rooster crows today, three times you will say that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: today a rooster will not crow: the day had begun at sunset, so before morning
decisions.reason: The Jewish day began in the evening. Before the roosters crowed near dawn, while it was still "today", Peter would deny Jesus.

decisions.choice: deny knowing me: say he does not know Jesus
alternatives: deny that Jesus is the Christ
decisions.reason: In 22:57-60 Peter says that he does not know him, not that he does not believe him.

decisions.choice: Peter: Jesus uses the name he gave Simon
decisions.reason: Only here in Luke does Jesus call him Peter, the name he gave him (6:14), meaning rock.

records.source: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅτε ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς ἄτερ βαλλαντίου καὶ πήρας καὶ ὑποδημάτων, μή τινος ὑστερήσατε;
records.gloss: And he said to them, When I sent you without money bag and bag and sandals, not anything did you lack?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "When I sent you out with no money bag, no traveler's bag and no sandals, were you short of anything?"

L.35: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "When I sent you out without money bag and bag and sandals, did you lack anything?"

R.35: Then Jesus asked them, "Remember when I sent you out without any money, travel bag or sandals? Did you need anything you did not have?"

decisions.choice: when I sent you: the earlier missions in Galilee
decisions.reason: Jesus sent the Twelve out with nothing for the road (9:3), and gave the seventy-two the same words, no money bag, no bag, no sandals (10:4).

decisions.choice: did you lack anything?: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The negative used here expects a no, and the apostles give it.

decisions.choice: bag: a traveler's bag for food and belongings
decisions.reason: The word means a leather bag carried on a journey.

records.heading: Purse, bag and sword

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οὐθενός.
records.gloss: They and said, Nothing.
pieces: They said, "Not a thing."

decisions.choice: nothing: God provided all they needed
decisions.reason: Their answer shows that the people they visited gave them what they needed.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἀλλὰ νῦν ὁ ἔχων βαλλάντιον ἀράτω, ὁμοίως καὶ πήραν, καὶ ὁ μὴ ἔχων πωλησάτω τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀγορασάτω μάχαιραν.
records.gloss: He said then to them, But now the [one] having a money bag let him take [it], likewise also a bag, and the [one] not having let him sell the cloak of him and let him buy a sword.
pieces: He said to them, "But now, whoever has a money bag must take it along, and a traveler's bag too. And whoever has no sword should sell {{gender:their|his}} cloak and buy one.

L.36: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "But now, let the one who has a money bag take [it], and likewise a bag; and let the one who does not have [one] sell {{gender:their|his}} cloak and buy a sword.

R.36: Jesus told them, "But now things are different. If you have money, take it with you. Take your travel bag too. And if you do not have a sword, sell your coat and buy one.

decisions.choice: the one who does not have: probably does not have a sword
alternatives: does not have a money bag
decisions.reason: The object is not stated. It may be the money bag (then he must raise money by selling his cloak), or the sword named at the end. Either way the cloak is sold to buy a sword.

decisions.choice: but now: a new time of danger and opposition
alternatives: the old instructions were a mistake
decisions.reason: Before, the disciples were welcomed; now their master is to be counted with criminals (22:37) and they will face hostility.

decisions.choice: sword: a short sword or long knife
decisions.reason: The word means a short sword or dagger. Whether Jesus meant real swords or spoke in a picture of the hostility ahead is debated; his reply in 22:38 and his rebuke in 22:51 suggest he did not mean them to fight.

decisions.choice: cloak: the outer garment, also used as a blanket at night
decisions.reason: Selling the cloak was a serious matter, since a poor man needed it (Exodus 22:26-27). The saying stresses how serious the danger is.

decisions.choice: whoever has no sword
alternatives: the one who does not have
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies the likely object (m1).

decisions.choice: now things are different
decisions.reason: Readable explains the contrast with 22:35 (m2).

records.source: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦτο τὸ γεγραμμένον δεῖ τελεσθῆναι ἐν ἐμοί, τό· Καὶ μετὰ ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη· καὶ γὰρ τὸ περὶ ἐμοῦ τέλος ἔχει.
records.gloss: I say for to you that this the having been written it is necessary to be fulfilled in me, the, And with lawless [ones] he was counted; and for the [things] concerning me an end has.
pieces: For I tell you, what is written must be fulfilled in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: 'He was counted among the lawless.' Yes, what was written about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is reaching its end."

L.37: For I tell you that this which has been written must be fulfilled in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: 'And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was counted with the lawless.' For indeed what concerns {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has an end."

R.37: I tell you, the Scriptures say, 'He was treated as a criminal.' This must come true about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Everything written about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is now coming true."

decisions.choice: he was counted with the lawless: Isaiah 53:12
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes Isaiah's servant of the Lord, who pours out his life to death, is counted with wrongdoers and bears the sin of many. Luke shows it fulfilled when Jesus is crucified between two criminals (23:32-33).

decisions.choice: has an end: is reaching its goal, is being fulfilled
alternatives: is about to be over and done with
decisions.reason: The word means end or goal. What is written about Jesus is coming to its fulfillment.

decisions.choice: must: God's plan, written in Scripture
alternatives: only what his enemies have decided
decisions.reason: Luke often uses "must" for what God has planned and Scripture foretells (24:26, 44).

decisions.choice: treated as a criminal
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase from Isaiah.

decisions.choice: what was written about me (B); everything written about me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the things are those written in Scripture, which the first half of the verse speaks of.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Κύριε, ἰδοὺ μάχαιραι ὧδε δύο.
records.gloss: They and said, Lord, look, swords here two.
pieces: They said, "Lord, look, here are two swords."

L.38: And they said, "Lord, look, here [are] two swords."

R.38: The apostles said, "Lord, look! We have two swords here."

decisions.choice: here are two swords: the apostles take Jesus' words literally
decisions.reason: They answer as though Jesus meant them to arm themselves now. His reply suggests they had missed his point (22:38b, 22:51).

decisions.choice: look (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the disciples point to the swords, so "look" is kept at every level.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἱκανόν ἐστιν.
records.gloss: He and said to them, Enough it is.
pieces: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "That is enough."

L.38: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "It is enough."

decisions.choice: it is enough: probably "enough of this talk", ending the conversation
alternatives: two swords are enough for what is needed
decisions.reason: If Jesus meant two swords were enough, he could not have meant armed resistance, since two swords could not defend a group. More likely he ends a conversation they have misunderstood, as in Deuteronomy 3:26 where God tells Moses, "Enough!"

records.source: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη κατὰ τὸ ἔθος εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν· ἠκολούθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταί.
records.gloss: And having gone out he went according to the custom to the Mount of the Olives; followed then him also the disciples.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left and went, as was {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} habit, to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.39: And going out, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went according to [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] custom to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples also followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.39: Then Jesus left the city and went to the Mount of Olives, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} usually did. His disciples went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: according to his custom: he spent his nights there during that week
decisions.reason: Luke has said that Jesus taught in the temple by day and spent the nights on the Mount of Olives (21:37). Judas therefore knew where to find him.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the ridge east of Jerusalem, across the Kidron valley
decisions.reason: The hill was named for its olive groves (19:29, 37). Luke does not name the garden or Gethsemane; he calls it "the place" (22:40).

records.heading: Not my will but yours

records.source: γενόμενος δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ τόπου εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Προσεύχεσθε μὴ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς πειρασμόν.
records.gloss: Having come then to the place he said to them, Pray not to enter into temptation.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} arrived at the place, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Pray that you do not come into temptation."

L.40: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to the place, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Pray not to enter into temptation."

R.40: When they reached the place, Jesus said to them, "Pray that you will not give in when you are tested."

decisions.choice: temptation: a time of testing that could make them fall away
alternatives: the final great trial at the end of the age
decisions.reason: The word means testing or temptation. Jesus has taught them to pray not to be led into temptation (11:4). Satan wants to sift them (22:31); tonight they will be tested.

decisions.choice: enter into temptation: be drawn into the testing and overcome by it
decisions.reason: To enter into temptation means to give way under it, not only to face it.

decisions.choice: give in when you are tested
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m2).

records.source: καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπεσπάσθη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λίθου βολήν, καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύχετο λέγων· Πάτερ, εἰ βούλει παρένεγκε τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ· πλὴν μὴ τὸ θέλημά μου ἀλλὰ τὸ σὸν γινέσθω.
records.gloss: And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and having placed the knees he was praying \v 42 saying, Father, if you are willing take away this the cup from me; yet not the will of me but the yours let be done.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went off from them about a stone's throw, knelt down, and began to pray,
"Father, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, remove this cup from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Yet let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done, not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}."

L.41: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and kneeling down {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying,
L.42: saying, "Father, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, take this cup away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; yet not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} will, but {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} be done."

R.41: Then Jesus went a short distance away from them, about as far as a person could throw a stone. He knelt down and prayed.
R.42: He said, "Father, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, take away this cup of suffering from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, not what I want."

decisions.choice: this cup: the suffering and death God has given him to bear
decisions.reason: In the prophets a cup stands for what God gives people to endure, often his anger against sin (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15). Jesus shrinks from it, yet accepts it.

decisions.choice: not my will, but yours be done: Jesus submits his own will to the Father's
alternatives: Jesus had no will of his own
decisions.reason: Jesus does not hide his wish to be spared, but he puts the Father's will first, as he taught in the prayer "your will be done" (Matthew 6:10).

decisions.choice: kneeling: a sign of earnest prayer
decisions.reason: Jews usually stood to pray (18:11, 13). Kneeling shows how urgent this prayer is (Acts 7:60; 20:36).

decisions.choice: was praying: he went on praying
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense shows prayer that continued.

decisions.choice: cup of suffering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup stands for (m1).

decisions.choice: about as far as a person could throw a stone
decisions.reason: Readable explains the measure.

records.source: ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ ἐνισχύων αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Appeared then to him an angel from heaven strengthening him.
pieces: Then an angel from heaven appeared to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} strength.

L.43: And an angel from heaven appeared to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, strengthening {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.43: Then an angel from heaven came to Jesus and made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} strong.

decisions.choice: 22:43-44 are part of the text (SBLGNT, without brackets)
alternatives: the verses are left out by several early manuscripts
some manuscripts mark them as doubtful or place them in Matthew 26
decisions.reason: The two verses are missing from several important early witnesses, among them Papyrus 75, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Alexandrinus and a corrector of Codex Sinaiticus; other early witnesses, among them the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Bezae and most later manuscripts, have them, and writers of the second century knew them. Some manuscripts mark them with signs of doubt, and some lectionary manuscripts read them after Matthew 26:39. Whether they were added, or left out by copyists who found them troubling, is much debated. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: strengthening: God answers his prayer by giving him strength, not by taking the cup away
alternatives: the angel freed him from suffering
decisions.reason: As angels served Jesus after his testing in the wilderness in other accounts (Mark 1:13), here God sends help to bear what he must face.

records.source: καὶ γενόμενος ἐν ἀγωνίᾳ ἐκτενέστερον προσηύχετο· καὶ ἐγένετο ὁ ἱδρὼς αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ θρόμβοι αἵματος καταβαίνοντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.
records.gloss: And having been in agony more earnestly he was praying; and became the sweat of him like great drops of blood falling down upon the ground.
pieces: In {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anguish {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prayed all the more intensely, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sweat became like thick drops of blood dripping down onto the ground.

L.44: And being in agony, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying more earnestly; and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sweat became like drops of blood falling down upon the ground.

R.44: Jesus was in great distress, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prayed even harder. His sweat was like large drops of blood falling to the ground.

decisions.choice: part of the text (SBLGNT), with 22:43
alternatives: left out by several early manuscripts
decisions.reason: See the note on 22:43. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: like drops of blood: his sweat fell like great drops of blood
alternatives: his sweat was mixed with real blood
decisions.reason: "Like" makes a comparison: the sweat fell in thick, heavy drops, as blood falls from a wound. The text does not say that it was blood, though some have read it so.

decisions.choice: agony: anguish, intense struggle
decisions.reason: The word means great distress of mind, such as an athlete or fighter feels before a contest.

decisions.choice: thick drops
decisions.reason: The word means a lump or clot; Balanced uses "thick" for drops that are heavy.

records.source: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἀπὸ τῆς προσευχῆς ἐλθὼν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εὗρεν κοιμωμένους αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί καθεύδετε;
records.gloss: And having risen up from the prayer, having come to the disciples he found sleeping them from the grief, \v 46 and he said to them, Why are you sleeping?
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up from prayer and came back to the disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them asleep, worn down by their grief.
And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why are you sleeping?

L.45: And rising up from prayer, coming to the disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping from grief,
L.46: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why are you sleeping?

R.45: Then Jesus got up from praying and went back to the disciples. He found them asleep, because they were so tired and sad.
R.46: He said to them, "Why are you sleeping?

decisions.choice: sleeping from grief: their sorrow wore them out
alternatives: they slept because they did not care
decisions.reason: Luke alone gives this reason; he treats the disciples gently. Deep sorrow can leave people exhausted.

decisions.choice: because they were so tired and sad
decisions.reason: Readable explains how grief led to sleep (m1).

records.source: ἀναστάντες προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν.
records.gloss: Having risen up pray, that not you may enter into temptation.
pieces: Get up and pray, so that you will not come into temptation."

L.46: Rise up [and] pray, so that you may not enter into temptation."

R.46: Get up and pray that you will not give in when you are tested."

decisions.choice: pray that you may not enter into temptation: the same command as in 22:40
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats his words from 22:40, so the scene begins and ends with the call to pray.

decisions.choice: give in when you are tested
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom, as in 22:40.

records.source: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ ὄχλος, καὶ ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα προήρχετο αὐτούς, καὶ ἤγγισεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ φιλῆσαι αὐτόν.
records.gloss: While still of him speaking, look, a crowd, and the [one] being called Judas, one of the Twelve, was going before them, and he drew near to the Jesus to kiss him.
pieces: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking, a crowd appeared. The man called Judas, one of the Twelve, was leading them, and he came up to Jesus to kiss {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.47: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking, look, a crowd [came], and the one called Judas, one of the Twelve, was going ahead of them; and he came near to Jesus to kiss {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.47: Jesus was still speaking when a crowd of people came. Judas, one of the twelve apostles, was leading them. He walked up to Jesus to kiss {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: to kiss him: the usual greeting of a disciple to his teacher
decisions.reason: A kiss was a common greeting among friends and from a pupil to a teacher. Mark says Judas had agreed to use it as a signal (Mark 14:44); Luke lets Jesus' words make the point (22:48).

decisions.choice: one of the Twelve: Luke repeats it to stress the betrayal
decisions.reason: Luke has already said this in 22:3; saying it again underlines that a chosen apostle led the arresting party.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence.

records.heading: Judas comes with a crowd

records.source: Ἰησοῦς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἰούδα, φιλήματι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδως;
records.gloss: Jesus then said to him, Judas, with a kiss the Son of the Man are you handing over?
pieces: But Jesus said to him, "Judas, is it with a kiss that you betray the Son of Man?"

L.48: But Jesus said to him, "Judas, with a kiss are you handing over the Son of Man?"

R.48: Jesus said to him, "Judas, are you using a kiss, a sign of friendship, to betray the Son of Man?"

decisions.choice: with a kiss: placed first, to stress the shock
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "with a kiss" first: a sign of love is used to betray.

decisions.choice: betray (B, R); handing over (L)
decisions.reason: As in 22:4, Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb.

decisions.choice: a sign of friendship
decisions.reason: Readable says what the kiss meant (m1 of 22:47).

records.source: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν τὸ ἐσόμενον εἶπαν· Κύριε, εἰ πατάξομεν ἐν μαχαίρῃ;
records.gloss: Having seen then those around him what would be, they said, Lord, if we will strike with sword?
pieces: When those around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw what was going to happen, they said, "Lord, should we strike with our swords?"

L.49: And when those around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw what was about to happen, they said, "Lord, shall we strike with [the] sword?"

R.49: Jesus' followers saw what was about to happen. They said, "Lord, should we fight them with our swords?"

decisions.choice: if we will strike: a direct question, asking permission
decisions.reason: In the Greek of this time "if" can introduce a direct question.

decisions.choice: those around him: the disciples with him
decisions.reason: These are the apostles who have the two swords (22:38).

records.source: καὶ ἐπάταξεν εἷς τις ἐξ αὐτῶν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τὸν δοῦλον καὶ ἀφεῖλεν τὸ οὖς αὐτοῦ τὸ δεξιόν.
records.gloss: And struck one certain of them of the high priest the slave and cut off the ear of him the right.
pieces: And one of them struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear.

L.50: And a certain one of them struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his right ear.

R.50: One of them swung his sword at the high priest's servant and cut off the man's right ear.

decisions.choice: slave: a slave owned by the high priest
decisions.reason: The word means a slave. As a high priest's slave he may have held some authority in the household. John gives his name as Malchus and says Peter struck him (John 18:10); Luke names neither.

decisions.choice: his right ear: Luke alone, with John, says which ear
decisions.reason: Luke the careful reporter gives the detail, which also prepares for the healing in 22:51.

decisions.choice: swung his sword at
decisions.reason: Readable says how he struck, from 22:49.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐᾶτε ἕως τούτου· καὶ ἁψάμενος τοῦ ὠτίου ἰάσατο αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Having answered then the Jesus said, Permit until this; and having touched the ear he healed him.
pieces: But Jesus said, "Enough of this!" And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched the man's ear and healed him.

L.51: But Jesus answered and said, "Permit [it] as far as this!" And touching the ear, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed him.

R.51: But Jesus said, "Stop! No more of this!" Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched the man's ear and healed him.

decisions.choice: permit as far as this: stop, that is enough
alternatives: let them go ahead and arrest me
let me reach the wounded man
decisions.reason: The words are short and unclear. Most likely Jesus tells the disciples to stop. They could also be spoken to those arresting him, asking them to put up with this one blow, or mean "let them have their way".

decisions.choice: he healed him: Jesus does good even to an enemy
decisions.reason: Only Luke tells of this healing. Jesus does what he taught: love your enemies and do good to those who hate you (6:27).

decisions.choice: [it]
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; Literal supplies one in brackets.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς τοὺς παραγενομένους ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ στρατηγοὺς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ πρεσβυτέρους· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων;
records.gloss: Said then Jesus to those having come against him, chief priests and captains of the temple and elders, As against a robber have you come out with swords and clubs?
pieces: Then Jesus said to the chief priests, the officers of the temple guard and the elders who had come out against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Did you have to come out with swords and clubs, as if I were a bandit?

L.52: Then Jesus said to the chief priests and captains of the temple and elders who had come against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?

R.52: Then Jesus spoke to the chief priests, the officers of the temple guard and the elders who had come to arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "Am I a bandit, that you have come out with swords and clubs to get {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

decisions.choice: robber: a bandit, or a violent rebel
decisions.reason: The word is used of armed robbers on the roads (10:30) and later of rebels against Rome. Jesus is treated like a dangerous man, though he taught openly every day (22:53).

decisions.choice: chief priests, captains of the temple, elders: the leaders of the council came themselves
decisions.reason: Luke says that some of the leaders were there in person with the arresting party.

decisions.choice: captains of the temple: the officers of the temple guard
the officers of the temple guard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the captains were (m3).

records.source: καθ’ ἡμέραν ὄντος μου μεθ’ ὑμῶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ οὐκ ἐξετείνατε τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ ἐμέ· ἀλλ’ αὕτη ἐστὶν ὑμῶν ἡ ὥρα καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ σκότους.
records.gloss: Every day being of me with you in the temple not you stretched out the hands against me; but this is of you the hour and the authority of the darkness.
pieces: Day after day I was with you in the temple, and you did not lift a hand against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness."

L.53: While I was with you every day in the temple, you did not stretch out [your] hands against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; but this is your hour, and the power of darkness."

R.53: Every day I was with you in the temple, and you did not try to arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But this is your time. This is when darkness is allowed to rule."

decisions.choice: your hour, and the power of darkness: God allows the leaders and the powers of evil a short time to act
alternatives: their power over Jesus is lasting
decisions.reason: "Darkness" stands for Satan's realm (Acts 26:18; Colossians 1:13). Satan is at work in the betrayal (22:3). This is their hour, but it is only an hour; God's plan stands (22:22).

decisions.choice: power: authority, the right to act
decisions.reason: The word means authority or power to act. It is the authority of darkness for this hour.

decisions.choice: every day: during the days he taught in the temple
decisions.reason: Jesus had taught in the temple each day since he entered Jerusalem (19:47; 21:37).

decisions.choice: try to arrest me
alternatives: stretch out your hands against me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: This is when darkness is allowed to rule
decisions.reason: Readable says the sense of the phrase in plain words (m1).

records.source: Συλλαβόντες δὲ αὐτὸν ἤγαγον καὶ εἰσήγαγον εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως· ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει μακρόθεν.
records.gloss: Having seized then him they led away and led into the house of the high priest; the and Peter was following from a distance.
pieces: They seized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away and brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into the high priest's house. Peter followed at a distance.

L.54: And seizing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they led [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away and brought [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] into the house of the high priest; and Peter was following from a distance.

R.54: They arrested Jesus and took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away to the high priest's house. Peter followed them, staying far behind.

decisions.choice: the high priest: Caiaphas, though Luke does not name him here
decisions.reason: Luke names Annas and Caiaphas together as high priests (3:2). Caiaphas held the office then (Matthew 26:57); John says Jesus was first taken to Annas (John 18:13).

decisions.choice: was following from a distance: Peter keeps near but out of sight
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows him following along. He keeps both his promise (22:33) and his distance.

records.heading: Peter's three denials

records.source: περιαψάντων δὲ πῦρ ἐν μέσῳ τῆς αὐλῆς καὶ συγκαθισάντων ἐκάθητο ὁ Πέτρος μέσος αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: Having kindled then a fire in middle of the courtyard and having sat down together, was sitting the Peter among them.
pieces: People had lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down around it, and Peter sat among them.

L.55: And when they had kindled a fire in [the] middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter was sitting among them.

R.55: Some people had made a fire in the middle of the courtyard. They sat down around it, and Peter sat with them.

decisions.choice: the courtyard: the open court inside the high priest's house
decisions.reason: Large houses were built around an open courtyard. The servants and guards waited there during the cold night (John 18:18).

records.source: ἰδοῦσα δὲ αὐτὸν παιδίσκη τις καθήμενον πρὸς τὸ φῶς καὶ ἀτενίσασα αὐτῷ εἶπεν· Καὶ οὗτος σὺν αὐτῷ ἦν·
records.gloss: Having seen then him a servant girl certain sitting toward the light and having looked intently at him said, Also this one with him was;
pieces: A servant girl saw him sitting in the firelight. She stared at him and said, "This man was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} too."

L.56: And a certain servant girl, seeing him sitting facing the light and looking intently at him, said, "This man also was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.56: A servant girl saw Peter sitting there in the light of the fire. She looked closely at him and said, "This man was with Jesus too!"

decisions.choice: the light: the light of the fire
decisions.reason: It was night; the fire lit up his face.

decisions.choice: servant girl: a young female slave or servant of the household
decisions.reason: The word is a diminutive of "child", used for a young slave woman (12:45). John says she kept the door (John 18:17).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus so that the reader can tell the men apart.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο λέγων· Οὐκ οἶδα αὐτόν, γύναι.
records.gloss: He but denied saying, Not I know him, woman.
pieces: But he denied it. "Woman, I do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}," he said.

L.57: But he denied [it], saying, "I do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, woman."

R.57: But Peter said that was not true. "Woman, I do not even know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!" he said.

decisions.choice: woman: a polite form of address
decisions.reason: Calling someone "woman" was ordinary and not rude in that culture (13:12).

decisions.choice: I do not know him: the first denial, as Jesus foretold
decisions.reason: Jesus said Peter would deny knowing him three times (22:34). The words match exactly.

records.source: καὶ μετὰ βραχὺ ἕτερος ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἔφη· Καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ· ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἔφη· Ἄνθρωπε, οὐκ εἰμί.
records.gloss: And after a little another having seen him was saying, Also you of them are; the but Peter was saying, Man, not I am.
pieces: A little later someone else saw him and said, "You are one of them too." But Peter said, "Friend, I am not."

L.58: And after a little [while], another [man] seeing him said, "You also are [one] of them." But Peter said, "Man, I am not."

R.58: A little later another person saw Peter and said, "You are one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers too!" But Peter said, "No, I am not!"

decisions.choice: another: another man
decisions.reason: The word is masculine, and Peter answers him as "Man". The other Gospels name other people who accused him.

decisions.choice: Man: a plain way to address a man one does not know
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same address in 12:14.

decisions.choice: Friend
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a neutral form of address, as in 12:14.

decisions.choice: one of his followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" were.

records.source: καὶ διαστάσης ὡσεὶ ὥρας μιᾶς ἄλλος τις διϊσχυρίζετο λέγων· Ἐπ’ ἀληθείας καὶ οὗτος μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἦν, καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν·
records.gloss: And having passed about hour one, another certain was insisting saying, Upon truth also this one with him was, for also a Galilean he is;
pieces: About an hour later another man insisted, "This is the truth: this fellow was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is a Galilean too."

L.59: And after about one hour had passed, a certain other [man] kept insisting, saying, "In truth this man also was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for he too is a Galilean."

R.59: About an hour later another man kept saying, "This is the truth: this man was with Jesus. He is from Galilee too!"

decisions.choice: in truth: certainly, surely
decisions.reason: A common phrase for stressing that something is so (4:25).

decisions.choice: a Galilean: someone from Galilee, known by his accent
